column1: # Per-workload perf baselines.
# Format (tab-separated):
#   <workload-path>\t<max_rss_kb>\t<max_wall_ms>\t<note>
# Workload paths are relative to the repository root. Lines starting
# with `#` are ignored.
# Two enforced metrics, both with the same ratchet etiquette:
#   max_rss_kb    Peak resident set size. The defended metric — see
#                 `docs/SUBSET.md` and `docs/adr/0010-...` for the
#                 "~5× lighter than CRuby" claim this guards. ≤5%
#                 noise across runs on the same machine, easy to
#                 threshold without flakiness.
#   max_wall_ms   End-to-end wall-clock time. Noisier than RSS but
#                 the second-most-important metric — rubyrs'
#                 dispatch-loop overhead is the visible cost.
#                 Set `0` to disable the wall-time check (use for
#                 sub-100ms workloads where measurement noise
#                 dominates).
# Bumping etiquette (identical for both columns):
# 1. Add a comment line above the row explaining *what grew* and
#    *whether it was intentional*. "Bumped because the new feature
#    X allocates Y" is fine. "Bumped to make CI green" is not —
#    investigate first.
# 2. Don't lower a budget silently. Lowering with a comment
#    ("workload X now runs at Y after Z's optimisation, tightening
#    from N → M") is the right move when a workload genuinely got
#    cheaper. Drive-by lowers erase historical ceilings.
# 3. Don't bump a budget to absorb a regression you didn't intend.
#    If the regression isn't part of the PR's stated change, treat
#    it as a separate bug.
# Why absolute baselines, not master-relative
# An earlier proposal was to compare each PR against `master` HEAD
# on the same runner ("PR's wall time must be ≤ 1.1× master's").
# That sounds tighter but it chain-degrades: if every PR is within
# 10% of "master at that moment", cumulative drift across N PRs is
# unbounded. Absolute baselines in this file are the same shape as
# the panic budget and the RSS budget — explicit, reviewable,
# committed to source. The cost is that the initial calibration
# numbers reflect a snapshot of one runner type; expect periodic
# re-cal commits when GitHub bumps the ubuntu-latest image.
# Initial calibration sources
# RSS observed on:
#   ubuntu-latest CI (PR #11 run 26383503758)  ~4.2-4.3 MB
#   local M-series Mac (release build)         ~3.0 MB
# Wall observed on:
#   ubuntu-latest CI (PR #11 run 26383503758)  fizzbuzz 0 ms,
#                                              mm 730 ms, dm 460 ms,
#                                              static 650 ms
#   local M-series Mac (release build)         fizzbuzz 0 ms,
#                                              mm 450 ms, dm 280 ms,
#                                              static 390 ms
# Headroom: budgets sit at ~1.3× the CI observation for RSS and
# ~1.5× for wall. RSS is tighter because it's the less-noisy
# metric (≤5% across runs); wall has a ~20-30% noise floor on
# the same CI runner, and the extra ~1.5× padding gives margin
# for occasional outliers without inviting flakes. Both should
# ratchet down further once a few stable CI runs accumulate.
# RSS bumped 5500→6500 (short workloads) / 6000→6500 (bench
# workloads) on 2026-05-27. Observed CI RSS across all eight
# workloads landed in the 6160–6404 KB cluster — a uniform
# ~700 KB step over the previous baseline. The growth attributes
# across recent master activity rather than any single PR:
#   - Preamble file count grew from 1 (inline raw-string PREAMBLE)
#     to 7 (.rb files: exceptions, object, comparable, match_data,
#     mutex, enumerable, plus the older random/securerandom/time).
#     Each adds parsed bytecode + Proto + class-shell metadata
#     loaded unconditionally at `Runtime::new`. The externalisation
#     itself (this branch's `aceebaf`...`0cacb96` series) is roughly
#     zero-cost in RSS — the same Ruby code moves from inline
#     string to file. The growth is from random/securerandom/time
#     PRs that added more vendor Ruby in absolute terms.
#   - BigInt phase B (`PR #138` to_s/sprintf, `PR #159` bit ops)
#     pulls in num-bigint static tables + more vm/bignum.rs
#     dispatch surface, even on bignum-off profiles via the no-op
#     stub functions.
#   - PR #167 (String batch ingestion) and PR #168 (String#count)
#     add ~3 KB each of string-method dispatch + the spec.rb
#     fixtures register via lazy loaders that still occupy table
#     entries.
# Set RSS to 6500 across the board (8 workloads) — gives
# 100–340 KB headroom over current observations without
# inflating the budget enough to mask a future regression.
# Per the bumping etiquette at the top of this file: this is
# "Bumped because the new features X allocate Y", not "bumped
# to make CI green".
# Uniform RSS bump 6500 → 6900 (+400) on 2026-05-31 across 6
# workloads (fizzbuzz, mm_bench, static_bench, fizzbuzz_1m,
# string_interp, hash_mutate). Observed CI RSS jumped ~150-300 KB
# on every workload after master accumulated several Tier-1 / ADR
# 0024 Phase A / Sinatra-PoC commits — preamble additions
# (`preamble/throw_catch.rb`, `preamble/match_data.rb`, etc. each
# `include_str!`-baked into the binary) and the Rust 1.95.0
# toolchain refresh both contribute. The growth is uniform across
# workloads, not localised to any specific feature, so a uniform
# bump is the right shape (vs the per-row dm/gc bumps above which
# tracked feature-specific regressions). 6900 leaves ~200 KB
# headroom over the observed CI peak (hash_mutate 6792); future
# regressions still surface.
# Uniform RSS bump 6900 → 7300 (+400) on 2026-06-03 across all
# 8 workloads. Observed CI RSS jumped ~30-220 KB on the bench
# workloads after `d397eaa2` (vm/per-invocation block-locals
# fix for the closure-in-iter capture bug surfaced by
# sinatra_plugin_smoke). The fix makes every `invoke_block`
# value-clone the captured locals Vec into a per-invocation
# fresh Rc — correctness win (the `.each { |s| -> { s } }`
# shape now returns per-iter values instead of last-iter
# leakage) at the cost of one extra Vec::clone per block
# invocation. Visible peaks: gc_churn 6900 → 7116 (200k
# short-lived allocations), static_bench 6900 → 6972 (2M
# block-frame invocations), string_interp 6900 → 7036.
# 7300 leaves ~180 KB headroom over the observed CI peak
# (gc_churn 7116); future regressions still surface. The
# trade is documented in `docs/SUBSET.md` §"Divergences from
# CRuby" / "Detached inner closures don't write-through to
# outer-method locals" — both shape AND cost recorded there.
# Uniform RSS bump 7300 → 7400 on 2026-06-06 for the four
# still-at-7300 workloads (fizzbuzz, mm_bench, fizzbuzz_1m,
# string_interp), matching the cohort already at 7400. The P3
# Jekyll-spike feature batch raised `Runtime::new` baseline RSS a
# few KB across every workload — new always-on preamble class shells
# (`Dir`, `RubyrsSass`), HashObj's two new fields (`class_tag` +
# `ivars` for Hash-subclass support), and a wider vm/dispatch +
# vm/lookup surface (Symbol methods, runtime attr_*, private_class_
# method, Dir/File primitives, …). fizzbuzz observed 7304 (4 KB over
# 7300); 7400 restores ~100 KB headroom without masking a real
# regression. Not "bumped to make CI green" — the features genuinely
# allocate the extra startup metadata.
# Bumped again after the Jekyll backlog (digest, regex named-captures,
# fileops write surface, Time.parse, the Hash O(1) index, …): the
# wider binary + the Hash index's per-Hash side map raise startup +
# allocation RSS across the board (CI observed fizzbuzz 7424,
# static 7408, string_interp 7448, hash_mutate 7476, gc_churn 7944).
# Two CI runs showed ~50-130 KB run-to-run variance right at 7500, so
# base workloads → 7700, hash_mutate → 7800 (index map), gc_churn →
# 8200 (observed 8072; mark/sweep over the new class-ivar +
# define_method roots) — ~150-200 KB headroom to absorb the jitter.
# Bumped the base RSS budgets 7700->7900 / 7800->7900 / gc_churn 8200->8400 by
# the session perf work (frame-locals pool, FxHasher, explicit-recv inline
# cache, BinOpLocalLocal superinstruction, ArgsBuf): the new code grew the
# binary, lifting baseline RSS ~80-100KB across all workloads (CI showed the
# 7700 group at 7612-7792, fizzbuzz tipping over). Pure baseline shift, not a
# per-workload leak — every workload moved up together.
# Uniform RSS bump 7900 → 8200 (+300) on 2026-06-08 across the seven
# 7900 workloads. The session's Enumerator finishing work grew the
# always-on preamble loaded at `Runtime::new`: preamble/float.rb (new
# file: Float::INFINITY / NAN / ...) and a much larger
# preamble/enumerator.rb (Enumerator#next/peek/rewind/size/to_h, the
# no-block→Enumerator helpers, and the ~130-line Enumerator::Lazy
# transducer class). More parsed bytecode + Proto + class-shell metadata
# at startup lifts baseline RSS uniformly. CI observed the 7900 group at
# 7752–7992 (static_bench 7992, fizzbuzz 7928 over). 8200 restores ~200 KB
# headroom over the observed peak without masking a future regression —
# a pure baseline shift (every workload moved up together), not a
# per-workload leak. gc_churn stays 8400 (observed 8216, has headroom).
# fizzbuzz RSS bumped 8200 → 8400 on 2026-06-10 — observed CI
# 8224 KB (24 KB / 0.3% over) after the ADR 0020 encoding series
# accumulated (EncodingTag on RStr, the compatibility arms in
# string.rs/heap.rs, String#byteslice — the cfg-gated
# _encoding_full code itself doesn't build here, but the always-on
# E1 surface grows the binary and lifts Runtime::new baseline RSS
# a few KB across the board). Same uniform-baseline-shift shape as
# every prior bump in this file; ~2% headroom over the observed
# peak so future regressions still surface.
# Uniform RSS bump on 2026-06-29 accepting the JIT-arc's accumulated
# base-runtime growth (maintainer decision). The previous 8400/8700/9400
# budgets predate the arc (last set 2026-06-14); observed CI RSS now
# clusters at 9096-9324 KB (gc_churn 10136) — a uniform ~700-800 KB step,
# beyond the file's ≤5% noise band. Attribution is diffuse across the
# ~500-commit arc (more always-on preambles baked via include_str!, the
# native-JIT codegen surface that compiles even on the jit-off default
# build via no-op stubs, generational-GC young/old bookkeeping). New
# budgets (9700 cluster / 10600 gc_churn — superseded 2026-07-04 by the
# 10900 cluster / 19000 gc_churn / 10600 boot recalibration below, which
# carries its own bisected diagnosis) leave ~400 KB headroom over the
# observed CI min so a real future regression still surfaces. This ACCEPTS
# the growth rather than optimising it — the '~5x lighter than CRuby'
# headline still holds with margin, but an RSS-reduction pass is worth
# scheduling as a follow-up.
# 2026-07-04 BUDGET RECALIBRATION (bisected on the Linux box, 8 build
# points 45e29f2c..aa2d0235; CI run 28722241462 corroborates within
# 20-280 KB): the campaign arc grew peak RSS in three knowing steps.
# (1) gc_churn +8.0 MB at a3073e5f — perf(gc) raised the GC
#     min-threshold floor 4096→32768 objects for the RuboCop wall
#     wins (require −28%, full run −25%); cost is linear at
#     ~250 B/floor-object and env-tunable via
#     RUBYRS_GC_MIN_THRESHOLD (=4096 recovers 17.9→11.7 MB).
#     Hash small-rep (429e4c3f, slot 168→136 B) clawed back 1.9 MB.
#     CLAWED BACK by the cost-proportional adaptive floor (heap.rs,
#     this branch): floor = clamp(16 × min(last two sweep µs),
#     4096, 32768) — churn workloads' cheap sweeps (~65µs) keep it
#     at 4096 while require-rubocop's expensive collections
#     (~2-3ms: root-gather + mark scale with loaded classes) pin it
#     at 32768. Box re-measure: gc_churn 18.0→11.5 MB with require
#     wall within noise of the static-32768 floor; gc_churn budget
#     dropped 19000→12000 below.
# (2) base rows +~1.3 MB tracking .text +1.26 MB resident code:
#     prism_wq +380 KB (RuboCop parser engine, compiled
#     unconditionally — cfg-gating it like jit_tier2 is the
#     ticketed clawback), snapshot.rs +264 KB (rides
#     preamble-cache), JSON campaign +228 KB, native encoding
#     constants +328 KB runtime (boot-perf lever, item-③ hash
#     capacity step included).
# Budgets below bumped to observed-CI + ~400 KB headroom; every
# row was green at wall (2-20x under) — this is an RSS-only recal.
# 2026-07-05 RE-TIGHTEN after the _prism_native gate (8352eab7): the
# default (CI) build no longer carries the RuboCop parser-engine port
# (.text -652 KB), measured clawback on the box: boot -472 KB, base
# rows -296~-436 KB. Budgets follow the clawback down so the ratchet
# keeps teeth; gc_churn stays 12500 (floor-dominated, -188 = noise).
crates/rubyrs/tests/fixtures/fizzbuzz.rb

column1: # mm_bench WALL bumped 1200 → 1300 on 2026-06-04 — observed
# CI 1220 ms (+1.7% over) after Track 1 / 2 chain accumulated:
#   * 0da682b3 (Track 1) — Frame::kw_given_mask: u64, +8 bytes
#     per frame; mm_bench pushes 2M frames so the extra word
#     load+store per push adds up.
#   * a65e3080 (Track 2) — Instance::frozen: Cell<bool>, +1
#     byte per Instance. mm_bench allocates Foo instances in
#     a tight loop; per-Instance write touches a cache line
#     the dispatcher just dirtied.
# Neither is hot-path slowdown individually; combined they
# push CI's already-tight 1200 ms cap over by ~20 ms. Same
# pattern as the existing hash_mutate / dm_bench / gc_churn
# WALL bumps above — bump to 1300 with ~80 ms headroom over
# observed peak, document the cause, leave the ratchet
# defending future bumps.
# Cross-bench WALL ratchet bump 2026-06-05 — observed CI:
#   mm_bench       1310 ms (cap 1300; +0.8%)
#   dm_bench        840 ms (cap  780; +7.7%)
#   static_bench   1070 ms (cap 1000; +7.0%)
#   gc_churn        360 ms (cap  320; +12.5%)
#   hash_mutate     810 ms (cap  800; +1.2%)
# Five benchmark workloads simultaneously breached WALL by
# 1-13% — exactly the runner-shift pattern documented for the
# 2026-05-27 round (hash_mutate / dm_bench / gc_churn moved
# together, no code regression). Same convention here: bump
# each row to ~7-10% above observed peak, leave the ratchet
# defending future bumps. Bumps recorded per row at the
# row-specific comment below.
# mm_bench WALL bumped 1400 → 1550 on 2026-06-09 — observed CI
# 1430 ms (cap 1400; +2.1%) after the `$!` dynamic-scope fix
# (commit 3134717c). Op::Return now does a `begin_rescue_depths`
# emptiness check on every method return to revert errinfo on a
# `return` out of a rescue body; mm_bench pops 2M frames, so the
# per-frame branch accumulates — same tiny-cost-×-2M-frames pattern
# as the 2026-06-04 / -06-05 bumps above. Within the documented
# 20-30% wall noise floor; bump to ~8% over observed peak, leave
# the ratchet defending future regressions.
# mm_bench RSS bumped 8200 → 8400 on 2026-06-10 — observed CI
# 8236 KB (cap 8200; +0.4%) after the Frame slimming (f2033e5b:
# the four inline Vecs moved behind Option<Box<FrameAux>>). The
# frames Vec's per-element footprint SHRANK (328 → 240 B), but the
# allocator's page mix shifted (size-class change for the frames
# backing buffer + per-aux boxes where begin/rescue runs) — a
# ~36 KB page-boundary effect, not a leak. 2026-07-04 note: the
# original attribution said "mimalloc size-class change", which is
# suspect — the CI perf-budget build is a plain default-feature
# `cargo build --release -p rubyrs` and runs the SYSTEM allocator
# (glibc malloc on ubuntu-latest), not mimalloc. The page-mix
# mechanism stands; the allocator named didn't build here. Joins
# fizzbuzz / hash_mutate at the 8400 tier (same 2026-06-10 rhythm).
crates/rubyrs/examples/metaprog_bench/mm_bench.rb
# dm_bench RSS bumped 6500 → 6700 on 2026-05-27 — the
# define_method dispatch benchmark crossed 6500 KB at PR #175
# (ic-stats baseline workloads added) + PR #178 (step-block
# iter refactor) + PR #179 (Array#delete). Observed CI RSS
# 6552 KB, ~52 KB over. The other 7 workloads stayed under
# 6500. Per-row bump rather than a uniform shift because the
# growth is dm-specific (define_method's closure surface
# touches the bumped tables); other workloads have their own
# headroom.
# dm_bench RSS bumped 7300 → 7400 on 2026-06-06 — the regex-flag
# carrier (CompiledRegex enum → struct with `source: Box<str>` +
# `ruby_flags`) grew the binary's static + per-regex footprint;
# CI observed dm_bench RSS 7316 KB, ~16 KB over. Same per-row
# rationale as the bumps above.
# dm_bench RSS bumped 8200 → 8400 on 2026-06-11 — observed CI 8216 KB
# (16 KB / 0.2% over) after the block-locals share-direct change
# (6b9c1fba) added a `captured_is_method_scope: bool` field to every
# BlockHandle. dm_bench is define_method-heavy (closure methods own a
# BlockHandle each), so the per-block byte + the wider dispatch.rs
# binary lift its startup/alloc RSS a hair over the razor-thin cap.
# Joins the 8400 cohort (fizzbuzz / mm_bench / hash_mutate); ~2%
# headroom over the observed peak.
crates/rubyrs/examples/metaprog_bench/dm_bench.rb
# static_bench RSS bumped 8200 → 8400 on 2026-06-11 — observed CI
# 8220 KB (20 KB / 0.24% over) after the merge-sort change
# (f57031a8). static_bench never sorts; the lift is the wider
# iter.rs/sort.rs binary on a runner image whose floors now sit at
# ~8.1–8.2 MB across ALL workloads (fizzbuzz read 8212 the same
# run). Joins the 8400 cohort (fizzbuzz / mm_bench / dm_bench /
# hash_mutate); ~2% headroom over the observed peak.
crates/rubyrs/examples/metaprog_bench/static_bench.rb
# Budgets at ~2× local M-series observed wall to absorb CI's
# ~1.65× ubuntu-latest slowdown plus per-run jitter — same shape
# as the metaprog rows above (static_bench: local 390ms / CI 650
# / budget 1000 = 2.5× local; mm_bench: 1.62× CI ratio observed).
# fizzbuzz_1m RSS bumped 8200 → 8400 on 2026-06-11 — observed CI
# 8208-8212 KB (8-12 KB / ~0.1% over a razor-thin cap) on BOTH
# 97e194ce (pre-arena, runner jitter at the boundary) and 26127917
# (Locals::Stack frame-locals arena: +8 B/Frame for the Locals enum
# + the persistent Vm::locals_arena buffer — a real but tiny
# baseline shift). Joins the fizzbuzz/mm/hash_mutate 8400 tier;
# ~2% headroom over the observed peak so future regressions still
# surface.

column1: # gc_churn RSS bumped 6500 → 6700 on 2026-05-27 — same
# direction as dm_bench's per-row bump above. Observed CI
# RSS 6504 KB (just 4 KB over) after PR #182 / #184 / #186
# accumulated. The 4 KB is well within run-to-run noise but
# the ratchet is absolute so it still trips. Bumping to
# 6700 gives ~200 KB headroom without inflating the cap
# enough to mask a future regression.
# gc_churn RSS bumped 7300 → 7400 on 2026-06-04 — observed
# CI RSS 7340 KB (40 KB over) after the Track 1/2/3 chain:
#   * 0da682b3 added `kw_given_mask: u64` to Frame (+8 bytes
#     per frame; gc_churn pushes ~200k frames across the run)
#   * a65e3080 added `frozen: Cell<bool>` to Instance (+1 byte
#     per Instance; gc_churn allocs Array+Hash heavily, not
#     Instance, so this row is dominated by the Frame growth)
# 100 KB headroom gives ~60 KB margin over observed CI peak
# without masking a future per-frame or per-instance bump.
# gc_churn RSS bumped 8400 → 8800 on 2026-06-08 — the full Enumerable
# module (preamble/enumerable.rb, ~40 methods built on #each) adds
# always-on Proto + class-shell metadata at Runtime::new that mark/sweep
# walks; CI observed gc_churn 8564 (164 over). The 8200 cohort stayed
# under (static_bench 7924 was the peak). Per-row bump (gc_churn-specific
# mark/sweep cost), ~236 KB headroom over the observed peak.
# gc_churn RSS bumped 8800 → 9000 on 2026-06-09 — observed CI 8804 KB
# (cap 8800; +0.05%, ONE 4 KB page over a razor-thin budget) on the
# carmine-crate commit, which doesn't even link into rubyrs — pure
# runner noise on an allocation-stress workload. Bump to ~2% headroom.
# gc_churn RSS bumped 9000 → 9400 on 2026-06-13 — the rack-spec push
# (Phases 1-7) grew the unconditional preamble ~450 KB (File::Stat +
# Dir methods, the zlib veneer, Time.rfc2822, tmpdir) which lifts every
# workload's baseline uniformly; gc_churn (the highest, alloc-stress
# peak) crossed at observed 9068 KB. Real preamble cost, not a leak —
# the other workloads stay well under 8400. ~3.5% headroom.
# gc_churn RSS dropped 19000 → 12000 on 2026-07-04 — the adaptive GC
# floor (see the campaign-recalibration note above) returns churn
# workloads to the 4096-object trigger window; box observed
# 11384-11700 KB across CI-default runs (min-of-3 semantics keep the
# check at the ~11.4-11.5 MB floor), so 12000 leaves ~500 KB headroom.
# Wall unchanged (observed 130-141 ms vs 400 budget): the extra sweeps
# the small window costs are ~65µs each on this workload's tiny live set.
crates/rubyrs/benches/gc_churn.rb

# (the base RSS every workload carries). The other 8400-cohort

crates/rubyrs/benches/hash_mutate.rb
# boot — base/startup RSS isolation (added 2026-06-29). Boot RSS is the
# FLOOR of all workloads (no per-workload churn), so its budget sits
# below the workload cluster: observed workload min was ~9096 (static_bench)
# pre-bump, and boot <= that. 9500 leaves ~400 KB headroom and is tighter
# than the 9700 cluster, so accumulated base-runtime growth trips THIS row
# first. Calibrated by reasoning (CI is the oracle) — tighten once the first
# CI run reports the actual Linux boot RSS. wall=0: boot is sub-100ms.
# 2026-07-05 boot 10200 -> 10450: the 10200 tighten (post-_prism_native
# clawback) was calibrated BEFORE three legitimate baseline additions
# landed on top: the fuzz-round reset fix's capture_baseline_contents
# deep copy (dfc846c3 — correctness: reset() rewinds preamble-slot
# mutations in place), M4's preamble/random.rb growth, and the M-wave
# baseline churn. CI observed 10,256; 10450 keeps ~200 KB headroom.
crates/rubyrs/benches/boot.rb
